topics.title: [DIS] FNN Safeguard — Recovery Verification and Pre-Upgrade Qualification for Fiber Nodes

recent_posts.topic_title: [DIS] FNN Safeguard — Recovery Verification and Pre-Upgrade Qualification for Fiber Nodes
recent_posts.author: Dappsoverapps
recent_posts.content_text:
Thanks for the feedback @quake The main value here isn’t just connecting existing backup tools. It’s making sure an FNN backup can actually restore the same node identity and channel/payment state, and letting operators test a new FNN version against a copy of their real node state before touching production.
That Fiber-specific recovery and upgrade verification is already the core of the proposal; the existing backup integrations are only supporting pieces.

recent_posts.topic_title: [DIS] FNN Safeguard — Recovery Verification and Pre-Upgrade Qualification for Fiber Nodes
recent_posts.author: ArthurZhang
recent_posts.content_text:
Just to clarify my perspective, I wasn’t previously familiar with this project and haven’t been involved in its design or development, so I can only comment as an outside observer based on the proposal and the discussion here.
Also I broadly agree with quake’s concern. The problem being addressed is legitimate, but much of the proposed work currently looks like integration and operational tooling around capabilities that already exist, rather than a sufficiently distinct technical contribution in its own right.
I also think the design could be specified more rigorously. For a system concerned with recovery verification and pre-upgrade qualification, it would help to define the relevant safety invariants, failure model, state-equivalence criteria, and upgrade/rollback semantics more explicitly, and then derive the implementation from those requirements.
So my concern is not that the problem is unimportant, but that I do not yet see enough technical differentiation or design rigour to justify treating this as a distinct safeguard system rather than an integration layer around existing FNN recovery and operational tooling.

topics.title: Asset Price Oracle on Nervos Network

recent_posts.topic_title: Asset Price Oracle on Nervos Network
recent_posts.author: ArthurZhang
recent_posts.content_text:
I think this is a genuinely useful direction for CKB.
The project-local feed cell + signed pull-update model feels much more natural for the Cell model than maintaining a globally shared mutable oracle cell. In particular, separating an untrusted transport/mirror layer from on-chain verification is a sensible design choice.
One point I would like to understand more clearly is the freshness model for permissionless consumers. If freshness is checked against a header dep, it would be useful to state the exact invariant that prevents an old but internally consistent oracle update from being paired with an old header. This seems particularly important for liquidation-style use cases.
There is also an important distinction between cryptographic oracle integrity and the economic integrity of the underlying markets. Given the relatively thin liquidity of some CKB markets, downstream protocols will probably need explicit exposure limits, confidence/deviation bounds, and perhaps spot/TWAP cross-checks rather than treating every correctly signed price as equally safe.
